newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY PLANS MOVE TO CONTAIN REBELLION

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) planned to frustrate any possible attempt by the rebels in Rajasthan to win over some more party legislators to their side. The party leaders have decided to keep all the party legislators together until the beginning of the brief assembly session on January 20. Sources said the BJP would organise a three-day workshop for legislators from January 17, during which all of them had been asked to stay at one place.
The Times Of India
PUNJAB POLL-EVE SCHEMES PUT ON HOLD

The Election Commission has rejected the Punjab government's demand to implement various welfare schemes notified on the eve of announcement of election on December 30, 1996. The election commissioner clarified that all normal activities of the government could continue, but any new decision directly intended to derive electoral advantage should be shunned. He said the commission had to ensure conditions existed for free and fair elections even before the announcement of elections and that the party in power did not take undue advantage of its position to influence voters.
The Pioneer
PLAN PANEL SEEKS TO TIGHTEN TAX NET

The Planning Commission has envisaged a scheme to tighten the tax net around higher income group which often manages to evade taxes with undisclosed sources of income. The panel has mooted a tax on visible expenditure. The proposal forms part of efforts to raise resources for the ninth Five Year Plan. Visible expenditure could be worked out by scanning luxury possessions such as flats, automobiles, cellular phones and air conditioners. The owners of such items could then be reassessed and made to pay a tax on the basis of the findings.
The Economic Times
SHAKEOUT LIKELY IN TELEVISION INDUSTRY

A crisis in the television broadcasting industry following a slump in advertising revenue may force a shakeout in the industry. While advertising on electronic media grew 60 percent in 1995 and an average 30 percent over the past five years, it rose only three percent in 1996. In absolute terms, advertising revenue grew by only 350 million rupees in 1996 as against 4.6 billion rupees in 1995. The growth appears to have been cornered by the state-owned broadcaster, whose advertising revenue grew by 30 percent in 1996.
GOVERNMENT TO GIVE 30 PCT SUBSIDY TO SHIPBUILDERS

In a move to give a fillip to the Indian shipbuilding industry, the Finance Ministry cleared a proposal to provide 30 percent subsidy to the ship builders. The subsidy would be provided to the shipyards over and above the cost of building a ship. Sources said the ministry had also approved certain other concessions to the shipbuilders without any major changes, primarily aimed at making the Indian shipyards internationally competitive.
ELECTRICITY ACT MAY BE AMENDED SOON

The Power Ministry is considering an amendment to the Electricity Act to ensure a higher rate of return for the private sector transmission projects. The act currently permits an assured return which is higher by five percent over the Reserve Bank of India lending rates. Sources said the power ministry was working out the details on the tariff issue and the procedures that would be adopted for finalising the transmission projects.
Financial Express
MINISTRY MULLS ARBITRATION BODY FOR FAST DISBURSAL

The Finance Ministry may set up an arbitration committee for speedy disbursal of funds locked in the securities scam. The committee, comprising representatives from banks, the income tax department and the custodian, is the culmination of lobbying by banks which lost billions of rupees in the scam. Banks contend they have nothing to gain from the distribution, as the 80 billion rupee tax demand exceeds the total cash of 34.66 billion rupees available with the notified parties. An expert group has assessed the exposure of banks and financial institutions at 31.05 billion rupees.
CROSLANDS TO MERGE WITH RANBAXY NOT PIRAMAL

The pharmaceutical manufacturers Ranbaxy and Croslands Research are discussing a merger proposal. Should the merger come through, the combined entity would have a turnover of 96 billion rupees. Analysts said the merger would place Croslands in safe hands in the long term. While details of the swap ratio in which the two companies would merge are not available, market sources said the firms are likely to merge in the ratio of 2.5 to 3 shares of Croslands for every share of Ranbaxy.
HYUNDAI PLANS 1,000 CC ACCENT

Sluggish sales in the mid-size car market have prompted Hyundai to rework its plans and enter with a smaller version of the Accent saloon car. The Korean auto giant is set to launch the 1000 cc hatchback Accent with an expected price tag of 350,000 rupees. Earlier, it had planned to launch two versions of the mid-sized 1,300 and 1,500 cc Accent.
Business Standard
BAJAJ AUTO ROPES IN CAGIVA TO DESIGN NEW SCOOTER

Bajaj Auto proposed to set up its third plant to manufacture two new models of scooters near Pune at a cost of four billion rupees. The new models would be equipped with four-stroke engines to adhere to pollution control norms. Chairman and managing director Rahul Bajaj said one of them would be designed by the company and would have manual transmission. The other model would be jointly designed by Bajaj Auto and Cagiva, an Italian company, also engaged in the manufacture of two-wheeelers, he said.
RELIANCE PLANS POLYPROPYLENE FIBRE UNIT

Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) is planning a polypropylene filament yarn and staple fibre (PPFY and PPSF) manufacturing facility. At present, only Neomar, Zenith, Sanghi and Gujarat Filament manufacture polypropylene staple fibre in India. The proposed downstream project is expected to be taken up in 1998 once the company commissions its second 400,000 tonne polypropylene unit. RIL plans to set up a 100,000 tonne per annum capacity of PPSF and PPFY at a cost of around five billion rupees.
The Observer
FOOD SUBSIDY SET TO CROSS 70 BLN RUPEES

Food subsidies are set to cross 70 billion rupees despite a claim by the food minister that it would be maintained at the budgeted level of 58.84 billion rupees. This will further add to the finance minister's woes who is finding it difficult to contain the fiscal deficit at 5.5 percent of gross domestic product, as no funds have come from disinvestment targeted at 50 billion rupees. The finance minister is pressing for a hike in the issue prices of foodgrains and sugar to rein in the subsidy. But political compulsions of the coalition United Front government are coming in the way. Such a decision would be taken only after Punjab elections in February.
